body.html: Who Chomna Resort is for — first, let's be clear: Chomna Resort isn't a luxury hotel in the middle of town with a fancy lobby, a rooftop pool and staff bustling everywhere · it's a small garden-house style resort of 21 rooms in Fai Kaeo subdistrict, Phu Phiang District, Nan Province, that sells rice-field surroundings, quiet, and a genuinely affordable price above all · its charm is that it captures the "Nan feeling" so many people are after — cottages set among green rice fields, fresh open air, quiet enough to hear nature, yet only about 1.5 km from Nan town, so it never feels like you've stranded yourself somewhere inconvenient · if we boil it down, this place suits couples who want a quiet stay with a nice atmosphere, families who drive themselves, budget travellers who want a base close to town and the airport, and people coming to Nan to make merit at the important temples, because it sits right on the road to Wat Phra That Chae Haeng · on the flip side, if you're after a hotel with a swimming pool, a gym, a spa or full five-star service, this place may not be your thing, because the heart of Chomna Resort is "a simple, clean, well-priced garden cottage," not luxury · that straight talk matters, because people who understand from the start that they're booking a small budget resort tend to leave happy, while those who slip into expecting a luxury hotel may feel something is missing

Location and getting around — this is Chomna Resort's number-one selling point, no doubt about it · the resort is at 10 Moo 17, Fai Kaeo subdistrict, Phu Phiang District, on the opposite bank of the Nan River from town, and what makes the location work is that it's just about 1.5 km from Nan town yet still gives you rice-field scenery and rural quiet · put simply, you get both — wake up to a rice-field view, but drive just a few minutes and you're at the town's restaurants, cafes and attractions · importantly, this location is on the road to Wat Phra That Chae Haeng, the pagoda for those born in the Year of the Rabbit and a sacred temple central to Nan, which makes it very convenient for people coming to pay their respects · for longer trips it still has the edge: it's only about 6 km from Nan Nakhon Airport (NNT), or about 13 min drive, so anyone flying in who wants to reach their stay quickly is well served · from the resort it's a short hop to the Wat Phumin area, the Nan walking street and the Nan National Museum, and about 10–15 minutes to drive up to Wat Phra That Khao Noi for the town view · the thing you have to accept, as with most stays on the outskirts of Nan, is that public transport in this area is limited, so having your own car, a rental car or a rented motorbike is the most convenient; without a car you'll rely on hired vehicles or ride-hailing apps, which aren't as common in Nan as in big cities, so allow extra time and plan ahead

"Lovely resort. The rooms are clean and leafy, the staff are friendly, and breakfast is tasty too · and the resort is easy to find, close to town, just a quick drive in to pay respects at Chae Haeng."

Room types and decor — Chomna Resort has 21 rooms in total, split into 5 types per the information given: single rooms (Standard), twin rooms (Standard Twin), triple rooms (Superior), family rooms (Family) and a villa · the good thing about having several types is the flexibility for groups of different sizes, from solo travellers to couples to a whole family · the decor is a simple garden-house style that prioritises cleanliness and practicality over luxury, with many rooms in separate cottages or low cottage rows that feel private and blend into the surrounding garden · the in-room amenities are complete for an overnight stay — air conditioning, TV, fridge, table and chairs, drinking water, and a private bathroom with the basics, and some rooms have a balcony or porch where you can sit and look out over the garden and rice fields · real reviews agree that the rooms are clean, tidy and the setting is leafy, which is something many budget stays don't manage consistently · one thing to know: because this is a cottage resort built and decorated bit by bit in a garden-house style, the details of each room may not be identical — size, bed layout, the view it faces, or whether it has a porch — so it's worth looking closely at the photos and details on the booking page, or asking the resort directly before you confirm, especially if you want a room that looks out over the rice fields or you're coming as a group

Amenities, garden and atmosphere — as a small budget cottage resort, Chomna Resort's amenities focus on covering the basics and the atmosphere rather than packing in extras like a big resort · what you definitely get is free Wi-Fi, parking, a garden, a restaurant and leafy common areas; the parking matters a lot for self-drivers, because you can park right up to your cottage easily, with none of the competition for spaces you get at a town hotel · the highlight many people mention is the rice-field and garden setting that wraps around the resort; the mornings are fresh and open, especially in the cool season when Nan is pleasantly cold, perfect for a stroll in the garden or sipping coffee while looking out at the fields · to be straight about it, there's no swimming pool, no gym and no spa here, because it's a small resort that sells simplicity, so anyone for whom a pool is a top priority should look at a resort with a pool in Nan town instead · but if what you want is a clean, quiet stay with a nice atmosphere, close to town and easy on the wallet, this level of amenities is plenty for one to three nights using it as a base for exploring Nan · the things worth checking with the resort in advance are the water heater in the bathroom, whether there's a sitting porch, and the restaurant's opening hours, so it all matches your expectations

Food and the restaurant — what sets Chomna Resort apart from the usual budget stay is that it has breakfast and a restaurant on site, which is a real advantage, especially in the morning when you don't have to rush off in search of food · real reviews mention the breakfast being tasty, which for a stay at this price is an impressive plus · some sources say breakfast is buffet-style, while at a small place like this it may at times be served as a set per the number of guests — so ask the resort about the breakfast format and serving times when you book or check in, just to be clear · for other meals, being close to Nan town helps a lot, because a few minutes' drive gets you to the town's restaurant and cafe scene, which has plenty to choose from, from khao soi and noodles to northern local dishes to nice cafes along the Nan River · so many people choose to eat breakfast at the resort for convenience, then head out to try the town's food for lunch and dinner · overall, food isn't the reason to come and eat in the resort, but having breakfast and a restaurant on site is a well-handled bonus that makes the stay easier, in keeping with the style of using the resort as a base to head out and explore Nan

Service and hospitality — for a small, family-run cottage resort, service is another point that earns praise in real reviews · guests agree that the staff are good, friendly and attentive, which is the charm of a small local stay that big chain hotels often can't match · owners and managers of local resorts in Nan tend to give good tips on attractions, restaurants and driving routes, because they really know the area · the thing to prepare for is that, being a small resort, there may not be staff at the counter 24 hours a day like at a big hotel, and per the information, check-in is from around 2:00 PM, with check-out from mid-morning to noon · so if you expect to arrive in Nan late or in the evening, you should tell them your arrival time and confirm a way to reach the resort in advance so check-in goes smoothly · overall, if you're used to staying at local resorts with a friendly, hands-on style, Chomna Resort's service will be predictable and more of a plus than a minus, but if you're used to hotels with a concierge on hand for everything around the clock, adjust your expectations from the start

What real reviews say (the praise and the gripes) — Chomna Resort is a small stay in Nan whose number of reviews on booking platforms isn't yet as large as at big hotels, so you have to read the overall picture from the guest voices that exist alongside what kind of place it is — a budget cottage resort · On the praise side: the most consistent feedback is that the rooms are clean, the setting is leafy and quiet, the staff are good and friendly, and breakfast is tasty · next is the location, which is easy to find and close to Nan town on the road to Wat Phra That Chae Haeng, making it convenient to get around, and the price that's very light for what you get · the rice-field views and garden-house feel are also something many guests are impressed by · On the watch-out side: the thing to understand from the start is that this is a small budget resort — no swimming pool, no gym or spa — and the amenities are basic · because these are garden cottages, the details and condition of each room may not be equal; some have better views, some are newer · and because it's in a semi-rural area on the outskirts, getting around without your own car will be a hassle, since public transport here is limited · most of these notes aren't really "downsides" but "the nature of a budget cottage resort in rural Nan" — understand them from the start and you can have a very satisfying stay at a price that's great value

"Stayed as a family. The room was spacious and clean, nice and quiet, and waking up to the rice fields was easy on the eyes · very cheap for what you get. The only gripe is there's no pool, and without your own car it's a bit of a hassle to get into town — but we drove ourselves so it was no problem."

Price and value — Chomna Resort's rates run from about THB 500–750/night and up for a standard room in the normal price range, which is very light for a stay this close to town and the airport, and the real price shifts with the season and room type, especially in the cool season (November–January), when Nan is a popular destination and accommodation across the province goes up, as well as during festivals and long weekends · compared with stays in Nan town, many of which start higher, or the rice-field-view resorts up the hills on the Pua District side that start in the thousands, Chomna Resort offers great value in terms of price for the cleanliness and location, especially for self-drivers who don't need a pool · if the heart of the trip is getting a clean stay with a nice atmosphere, close to town and the important temples, on a budget that leaves money for good food and more sightseeing, this place gives you what you want and is worth every baht · but if you put a premium on a pool, sweeping terraced rice-field views, or hotel-level service, another type of stay at a higher budget may feel like better value · the tip is to compare prices on Agoda and Trip.com side by side, because for a small stay like this the price and cancellation terms sometimes differ between platforms, and at times there are promotions starting at around THB 500

Things to know before you book — a few things help make a stay at Chomna Resort go more smoothly · one, get the format right — this is a budget garden-cottage resort, not a luxury hotel, so there's no pool, gym or spa, but you do get cleanliness, quiet, a rice-field setting and a good price · two, have your own car or rent one, because it's in the semi-rural Phu Phiang outskirts and public transport is limited; having a car makes exploring Nan the most convenient · three, tell them your arrival time in advance, especially if you expect to reach Nan in the evening, since check-in is from the afternoon and there may not be a 24-hour counter · four, if you want a rice-field-view room or you're coming as a group, ask about the room types and bed setup clearly, because there are several types with different details · five, ask about the breakfast format and times so you can plan your morning meal before heading out · six, book ahead in the cool season and during festivals, because Nan gets busy and accommodation fills up fast · seven, choose free cancellation to be safe if your plans aren't firm, and compare prices on both Agoda and Trip.com before you book

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Chomna Resort is the best fit for people who want a place to stay in Nan with rice-field surroundings, clean, quiet, close to town and the airport, on a budget · being a 21-room garden-cottage resort just 1.5 km from town on the road to Wat Phra That Chae Haeng makes it work for couples, families and self-drivers, with a well-praised breakfast and good service as pluses · but you have to accept honestly that it's a small budget resort, not a luxury hotel — no swimming pool, no gym or spa, and you need your own car to get around easily · if you're looking for a pool, full service, or sweeping terraced hill rice-field views as the heart of the trip, a stay in Nan town or a rice-field-view resort on the Pua side may suit you better · but if you understand and like the simple garden-cottage format, and want cleanliness, quiet, a rice-field setting and a location close to town at one of the lightest prices in Nan — Chomna Resort is a small place that does its job well and is more than worth the price

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Chomna Resort, Nan

faq.q: Where is Chomna Resort · is it far from Nan town?
faq.a: The resort is at 10 Moo 17, Fai Kaeo, Phu Phiang District, Nan · it's just about 1.5 km from Nan town, on the road to Wat Phra That Chae Haeng, and about 6 km from Nan Nakhon Airport (about 13 min drive) · you can drive into the Wat Phumin area and the Nan walking street in a few minutes, making it a good base for exploring Nan town; you should have your own car or rent one

faq.q: What kind of place is Chomna Resort · how many room types are there?
faq.a: It's a small garden-house style resort with 21 rooms, with 5 types to choose from: single, twin, triple, family and villa · every room has air conditioning, TV, fridge, drinking water, table and chairs, and a private bathroom · the focus is on cleanliness, simplicity and quiet rice-field surroundings

faq.q: What's the starting price at Chomna Resort · where do you book?
faq.a: Rates start at about THB 500–750/night for a standard room in the normal price range, which is very light for a location this close to town and the airport · the real price shifts with the season, especially the cool season (Nov–Jan) and festivals · you can book via Agoda and Trip.com; we'd suggest comparing prices on both platforms and checking the cancellation terms before you book

faq.q: Does Chomna Resort have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool, because it's a budget cottage resort · but there is breakfast that real reviews call tasty, plus a restaurant, a garden, parking and free Wi-Fi · if you want a pool, consider a hotel in Nan town that has one instead

It's a great fit for couples, families and budget travellers who drive themselves and want a clean, quiet stay with rice-field surroundings, close to town and Nan's important temples · if you're looking for a pool, luxury-hotel service, or sweeping terraced hill rice-field views, a hotel in town or a rice-field-view resort on the Pua District side may suit you better
